title: Studying effect of hypergravity on cleavage timings in developing embryos of _Limnaea_
protocol: Include the ANSI C++ algorithm in Turbo C++ v.3.0 software for calculating correlation between real time hypergravity values and centrifugal speed (RPM).
Enter the program "Program for Calculation of Centrifugal RPM with respect to Hypergravity" into Turbo C++ v.3.0.
Input the average radius (r) of the centrifugal tube in the algorithm.
Calculate the constant b using the formula e*r, where e = 0.00001119.
Enter the value of hypergravity (RCF) required for the experiment into the algorithm.
Compute revolutions per minute (rpm) using the calculated RCF and constant b.
Output the calculated RPM value from the program.
Repeat the process until all necessary RPM values are calculated for different RCF inputs.
Enter the algorithm into the software.
Run the program.
Input the average radius \(r\) of the centrifugation rotors provided by the manufacturer.
Input the required value of hypergravity based on the type of investigation.
Use specific values for hypergravity such as +9G, +8G, +4G, or +20G depending on the nature of the investigation.
The program calculates and provides the corresponding RPM value.
Run the ultracentrifuge at the calculated RPM.
Visit freshwater ponds with floating lotus or water lily leaves.
Turn the leaves upside-down and observe for presence of transparent egg masses attached on the leaves under surface.
Identify and confirm the taxonomic status of _Limnaea_ snails.
Bring these _Limnaea_ snails and the leaves along with the pond water to laboratory.
Filter the pond water and fill it into troughs.
Lay down the lotus leaves on the water's surface.
Allow the snails to lay eggs under the leaves.
Detach egg masses carefully from the leaf’s under-surface using a scalpel or forceps.
Transfer detached egg masses into a Petri dish containing filtered pond water.
Observe various eggs under the light microscope.
Segregate each of them into specific groups depending upon the developmental stage in which the embryo exists.
Note the time intervals between various cleavages.
Put the eggs into the centrifuge tube once the cleavage stage is identified.
Centrifuge the eggs in an ultracentrifuge at the calculated RPM speed.
Note the time of exposure to centrifugation for the eggs.
Remove the eggs from the centrifuge when the expected cleavage stage should be reached based on previous timings.
Immediately observe the eggs under a light microscope to check if the expected cleavage stage has occurred.
Record the timings and analyze the values for each cleavage stage in both normal and hypergravity conditions.
